title: New Aligned Delegates face immediate derecognition for a procedural breach during a 90-day probation
content:
A.1.6.1.4 establishes a Probationary Period — "the first 90 days following recognition" — during which "the Core Facilitator applies heightened accountability standards." A.1.6.1.4.1 specifies what that means concretely: a Tier 1 (Procedural) breach "results in immediate derecognition without the requirement of a prior formal warning."

The mechanism is subtractive rather than additive. Nothing new is prohibited during probation; what changes is that the graduated response framework's first step is removed. Outside probation, a procedural breach earns a warning before escalation; inside it, the same breach ends the delegateship.

The reasoning is about *screening* rather than punishment. Tier 1 breaches are procedural — missed participation thresholds, late or inadequate vote explanations — and an actor who cannot meet basic procedural obligations in their first three months is signalling either an inability or an unwillingness to do the role. Catching that during probation is far cheaper than after the delegate has accumulated delegated voting power and a voting record.

It also compensates for how little the recognition process screens. A.1.6.1.3 requires no interview, credentials, or track record — only a deployed contract and two valid signatures. Entry is deliberately permissionless and cryptographic, so the quality filter has to sit *after* admission. Probation is where that filter lives.

The cost is asymmetric severity for identical conduct: a first-week lapse is terminal, an identical lapse in month four is a warning. That is defensible as a bargain the applicant accepts knowingly, but it means the population of long-serving delegates is partly selected by having survived a period when the rules were strictest.
description: A.1.6.1.4.1 removes the prior-formal-warning step that Tier 1 breaches normally carry, making the graduated response framework inapplicable for the first 90 days after recognition.
